Q: How to implement online runner for JavaScript? A:

I don't think it can be easily answered. For that you would need to build fully fledged web app.

So you would need frontend to server UI and then backend server.

The actual work would be done in the backend, where you would process code that user has entered, detect language, attach debugger. Then you would also need to "bridge" frontend app to the debugger, so user on web page could debug his code.

However, your question is just too broad to be answered. There is not any tutorial nor library that you would just install and use.

Q: How to write subquery in select list in EF Core? A:

The SQL query is wrong and this is a misuse of EF Core.

First, that SQL will fail if there's more than 1 result from the subquery. Even in SQL you'd need a different query. An INNER JOIN would return the same results without failing if there are multiple matches.

Select s.*,ps.DefaultStartDay 
from Scheduler.Schedules s
    inner join Scheduler.ProgramSettings ps on ps.DefaultStartDay = s.Id
where ScheduleType = 2;

Second, using LINQ to emulate SQL is a misuse of both EF Core and LINQ. EF isn't a replacement for SQL, it's an ORM. Its job is to give the impression of working with in-memory objects instead of tables, not allow you to write SQL queries in C#

It's the ORM's job to generate JOINs as needed from the relations between entities (not tables). In this case, if Schedule has a ProgramSettings property, EF would generate the necessary joins automatically. Loading an entire schedule object could be as simple as:

var schedules=_context.Schedules
                      .Incule(sch => sch.ProgramSettings)
                      .Where(s => s.ScheduleType == 2)
                      .ToArray();

Include is used to eagerly load the settings, not to force a JOIN.

If a Select clause is used that requires a property from ProgramSettings, the JOIN will be generated automatically, eg :

var namesAndDays=_context.Schedules
                      .Where(s => s.ScheduleType == 2)
                      .Select(s => new { 
                          Name = s.Name,
                          StartDay = s.ProgramSettings.DefaultStartDay 
                      })
                      .ToArray();

Q: ASP.NET Core MVC area scaffolding fails with “Package restore failed” on .NET 8 A:

If package roll back happens, 1st you need check all your installed packages up to date, and if you're using EF Core keep all packages related to EF Core as same version, then do the scaffolding.

Q: My code gets stuck at the end of the prepare_for_answer function. Is there something really obvious I'm missing? A:

I don't know anything about turtle graphics, but something looks suspiciously wrong with your code.

You start of calling main_8_ball, which then calls turtle_prepare_for_answer, which then calls main_8_ball again. You end up in an endless recursive loop that will eventually exhaust memory or cause some other internal error with turtle graphics logic.

Since you have a while loop_setter==1: loop that repeatedly calls main_8_ball, but which never currently returns, at the very least remove the call to main_8_ball at the end of function turtle_prepare_for_answer.
